static_traits.name: Zhou Yannan
static_traits.occupation: Having worked the same job for 8 years
static_traits.family_status: Mother is a Nurse; the rest Not mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Has friends to talk with, but often feels they will not understand my unease about guitar playing; other details of Interpersonal relationships Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: The client tends to negate the positive in guitar playing and overgeneralize mistakes; any small error markedly raises stress, making them feel like a 'terrible guitarist', more prominent lately, even starting to affect self-esteem and confidence in other abilities.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizing negative thoughts affect self-esteem and enjoyment of music, thus hoping to learn to identify and challenge these negative thoughts, regaining a more balanced perspective and the joy of playing.

special_situations.event: Missed a note while playing one's favorite song
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I still make mistakes in familiar pieces, it proves I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Practicing twice as much to avoid any mistakes, and repeatedly correcting every error

special_situations.event: A small mistake occurring during performance or practice even when overall performance is Good
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as there is a mistake, none of the good parts count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing attention on mistakes, negating positive performance and others' praise
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those good parts do not matter

special_situations.event: After a minor mistake in practice, begins to doubt her abilities in other areas
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One mistake means my overall ability is inadequate
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Defines oneself with negative labels, reducing willingness to take challenges
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I cannot even play this well, I will fail at other things too

special_situations.event: When thinking of discussing unease about guitar playing with friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they do not understand, it means I should not express my unease
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding discussing related unease and troubles with friends

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as a capable performer, and to regain the pleasure and self-esteem of performing
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated after mistakes, being seen as not good enough, thereby Impaired self-esteem
defense_goal: Avoids failure and others' evaluations through harsh self-judgment
Staying cautious and somewhat distant to avoid the experience of not being understood

object_relations.self_representation: An unqualified performer prone to failure
A person who tries hard but easily negates their own strengths
object_relations.object_representation: Others who give praise but are seen by me as unimportant others

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When considering talking to friends about my playing unease and sense of failure
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing friends will not understand my feelings (transference: Projecting my own unease as others not understanding)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a euphemistic tone that avoids depth, quickly ending the topic or shifting to other content, e.g. 'forget it, they will not understand', reducing self-disclosure.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others or I notice most passages played Good but small mistakes still occur
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing this one mistake Undoing all positive performance, praise not genuine or not important
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Negating strengths with seemingly rational statements, like 'that was just luck' 'one mistake means not good', in a calm but firm tone.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When a mistake occurs in a familiar piece
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizing the external standard of zero errors into self-evaluation, believing one must be perfect to be competent
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes wording such as 'should' and 'must', engages in harsh self-criticism, reduces emotional expression and self-acceptance.

manifestations: Playing is no longer a pleasure but a source of stress
Excessive focus on mistakes erases positive experiences and sense of achievement
Feeling friends will not understand my unease, thus sharing less

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Over-focusing on mistakes and being harsh on oneself
Judges the performance by the perfect standard of 'should/must'
Being cautious when talking about unease, constricting self-expression

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Believing friends will not understand my guitar unease, thus Avoids communication

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy originally to be emitted outward by instinct toward oneself.
manifestations: Not seeking understanding and support from others, instead increasing practice and self-criticism

exception_events.target_problem: When playing familiar pieces, once a small error occurs, the client usually Self-deprecates, Rising stress, and negates positive performance
exception_events.unique_outcome: Sometimes the client plays Good and receives others' praise, and can admit 'I did play quite well' rather than fully negating
exception_events.reason: Different support and situation: playing familiar songs, long-term practice building a skill foundation, and receiving others' positive feedback, helping them briefly see a fuller picture of performance

positive_force: Having friends who can offer some support
Able to identify and name negative cognitive patterns (negating the positive, overgeneralization, etc.)
Willing to seek psychological counseling and try new strategies (listening back to recordings)
Persisting in guitar practice, having a skill foundation
negative_force: Negating positive thinking, struggling to integrate positive evidence
Overgeneralizing a single mistake as inadequate overall ability
Assuming others will not understand and thus avoiding Social support

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecation and negative self-talk when small errors occur in playing (like 'I am a terrible guitarist') accompanied by rising stress
antecedent: Making mistakes when playing a favorite song
After receiving positive feedback from others, still notices one small mistake
target_behavior.core_reason: Based on all-or-nothing perfection standards and negating-the-positive thinking, equating a single mistake with inadequate overall ability and tying it to self-worth
target_behavior.function: Trying to control and avoid future mistakes through self-criticism, escaping the risk of being seen as 'not good enough'
target_behavior.consequence: Rising stress, declining joy of playing, Impaired self-esteem, and starting to doubt abilities in other areas; less communication with friends about playing unease
